A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MFAR study and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Renamed models and relocated material can be matched; some v2 results have internal reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: v1 reports original STaRK retrieval experiments, query-conditioning and field-masking ablations, and qualitative analyses, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds representation-combination experiments, random-seed variability, BM25F comparisons, and NQ-Tables evaluation.

M1.justification: v2 adds MFARLexical+1, MFARDense+1, and MFARAll+2, augmenting field-level scoring with whole-document scorers (Appendix C.2). The underlying loss, adaptive weighting, normalization, and inference procedure remain unchanged. v1's MFAR1+n corresponds to v2's MFARDense&1, rather than being a newly introduced method.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds NQ-Tables evaluation over 170K Wikipedia tables, decomposed into titles, column headers, and table content. This extends coverage from the three retained STaRK knowledge-graph corpora to a distinct tabular retrieval task with substantially different document structure.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated BM25F comparator against BM25 and MFARAll on STaRK (Table 12), and DPR-table 110M against MFAR variants on NQ-Tables (Table 16). The original STaRK baseline set remains; BM25F's earlier citation alone did not constitute an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The original STaRK splits, sequence limits, batch sizes, and evaluation metrics are retained. Added experiments use uniformly weighted BM25F, reuse corresponding base-model hyperparameters for new MFAR variants, and evaluate NQ-Tables at R@1/5/10/20 without a new hyperparameter sweep.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 and Table 10 add a focused analysis of whether whole-document lexical or dense representations improve their field-level counterparts. The original query-conditioning ablation, scorer and field masking, and qualitative examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-seed uncertainty analysis. v2 Appendix C.3 explicitly reports retraining with three additional random seeds, distinct from the main experiment seed, and Table 11 reports standard deviations across datasets and metrics for six MFAR variants. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, although no formal significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial variant, BM25F, and NQ-Tables results while retaining the original core STaRK rows. Table 16 reports MFARAll R@1/R@20 of 0.498/0.949 versus DPR-table's 0.679/0.906. Combined-model attribution is inconsistent: Tables 1 and 8 label a row MFARAll+2 that Table 10 assigns to MFARDense&1, while giving MFARAll+2 different values. These conflicting entries prevent a reliable cross-version performance comparison for the renamed MFAR1+n configuration.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same contrastive objectives and adaptive scoring formulation. Explicit negative-set and batch notation, the reverse-loss rename, and clarification of embedding dimensions explain existing mathematics. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: flexible hybrid multi-field retrieval, query-conditioned weighting, strong STaRK performance, and interpretable field analyses. Replacing 'structured' with 'semi-structured' refines terminology for the same defined documents without materially redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds applicability qualifications concerning short tables, few fields, Wikipedia pretraining exposure, and weaker top-1 performance despite stronger deeper recall. Appendix D attributes weak uniformly weighted BM25F results to potentially suboptimal weights and discusses tuning costs. These substantive qualifications are absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository link, explicitly states that the adaptation function shares the query/document encoder, and documents hyperparameter reuse for added variants and the BM25F implementation source. Existing hardware, software versions, learning-rate grids, and inference shortlist details are largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 expands positioning relative to table retrieval, including Herzig et al. and Wang et al., and alternative hybrid representation methods, including Lin and Lin and Shen et al. The central distinction based on shared end-to-end training remains. Publication updates to retained works, such as Wikiformer, are bibliographic changes rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 polishes introductory and methodological prose, repairs the malformed qualitative explanation, consistently adopts 'semi-structured,' reorganizes related-work paragraphs, and adds appendix subsections and acknowledgements. Author affiliations and publication headers change, while the main scientific section order is retained.

P2.justification: The three figures and existing table designs are retained. Four new tables display representation combinations, seed variability, BM25F, and NQ-Tables results. Dataset statistics move from the main text to Appendix A, with additional table relocation, caption editing, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: With the original evidence retained, additional-seed variability, an evaluation exposing table-retrieval limitations, and a project repository link make v2 more informative and reproducible. The net gain is limited by conflicting MFARAll+2/MFARDense&1 result attribution across Tables 1/8 and 10, and BM25's inconsistent MAG MRR: 0.472 in Table 12 versus 0.572 in Table 1. These problems weaken confidence in parts of the added comparisons.
